body:
### Summary

There is currently no way for a **project to advertise how it should be run** under `uvx` (`uv tool run`) when it doesn't ship a console script named after its normalized distribution name. `uvx` will only launch a package by an executable whose name equals the PEP 503-normalized project name, so a project that wants to expose its functionality *under its own package name* is pushed to either:

1. declare a `[project.scripts]` console script whose key is the mangled normalized name (e.g. a package named `coherent.cli` must ship a script literally named `coherent-cli` — the canonical dotted name can't be used as the command), or
2. force every caller into the verbose form:

   ```console
   uvx --from coherent.cli python -m coherent.cli build
   ```

Compare with pipx, where the project advertises its run target once (via the `[pipx.run]` entry-point group) and callers get the elegant:

   ```console
   pipx run coherent.cli build
   ```

The `uvx` equivalent today is much less ergonomic for exactly the projects that model their command as `python -m <package>` (the [documented package entry point](https://docs.python.org/3/library/__main__.html#main-py-in-python-packages)) rather than a separately-named script.

### Request

Let a project **declare a default run target** that `uvx` will honor, so that

```console
uvx coherent.cli build
```

resolves to the project's advertised entry point (e.g. `python -m coherent.cli`, or a `module:callable`) **without** requiring a console script whose name matches the normalized distribution name.

Possible shapes (open to whatever fits uv's model):

- Honor an entry-point group, à la pipx's `[pipx.run]`:

  ```ini
  [pipx.run]          # or a uv-native group name
  coherent.cli = coherent.cli.__main__:app
  ```

- A `uv`-native metadata field, e.g. in `[tool.uv]`, naming a module or `module:callable` to run when the package is invoked by name.
- As a sensible default, when a package provides a `__main__.py` and no matching console script, run `python -m <package>` (this alone would cover a large fraction of cases).

### Prior art / ergonomics gap

pipx solved this with `[pipx.run]`: a project declares a module/callable and `pipx run <name> <args>` works. With pipx now auto-selecting its **uv backend** whenever `uv` is present, that mechanism is bypassed (`uv tool run` has no notion of `[pipx.run]`), so packages relying on it become unrunnable via `pipx run` — see pypa/pipx#2004. A first-class uv way for a project to advertise its run command would close that gap and remove the need for `--from <pkg> python -m <pkg>` boilerplate.

### Relationship to #7552

#7552 ("Module support for uvx") requests a **caller-side** shorthand (`uvx <pkg> -m <module>`), where the invoker still names the module. This issue is the **project-side** complement: the package advertises its run target once, so the caller can just write `uvx <pkg> <args>` and needn't know or spell the module. The two compose well — caller-side `-m` for ad-hoc use, project-side declaration for packages that want `uvx <name>` to "just work".

### Example projects affected

Any package whose natural command is `python -m <package>` and whose module name differs from (or is a dotted form of) the normalized dist name — e.g. `coherent.cli` / `coherent.test`, and the modules called out in #7552 (`setuptools_scm`, `grpc_tools.protoc`).
title: Let a project advertise its run target to uvx (project-side equivalent of pipx's [pipx.run])
